nameStory: Gonatozygon kinahanii doesn't have a widely-used common name since it's a microscopic algae that most people never see without a magnifier. The scientific name comes from Greek words meaning 'angled yoke,' referring to how these tiny cells connect together like oxen joined by a wooden yoke. Named after Kinahan, likely an early botanist who studied these minute water dwellers.
description: This is a microscopic green algae that lives in freshwater ponds, streams, and wet soil throughout New England. **[UNCERTAIN: Specific morphological details]** Each individual cell is so tiny you'd need a hand lens or microscope to see it clearly, but colonies might appear as greenish films or threads in very still water. Unlike the plants most people think of, this algae has no roots, stems, or leaves - just simple cells that can photosynthesize like plants do.

idTips.label: Aquatic habitat
idTips.description: Found in very still freshwater - look for greenish films or threads in quiet pond edges or slow-moving stream backwaters

idTips.label: Cell connection

habitat: **[UNCERTAIN: Specific habitat preferences]** Found in quiet freshwater environments across New England, including pond margins, slow streams, temporary pools, and very wet soil. Prefers areas with little water movement where it can form stable colonies without being washed away.

seasonality.spring: **[UNCERTAIN: Seasonal patterns]** May become more visible as water temperatures warm and daylight increases, potentially forming more noticeable colonies.
seasonality.summer: Peak growing season when colonies are most likely to be visible as greenish films on quiet water surfaces.
seasonality.fall: **[UNCERTAIN: Fall behavior]** Populations may decline as temperatures drop and daylight decreases.
seasonality.winter: **[UNCERTAIN: Winter survival]** Likely survives as dormant cells or resistant stages in sediments under ice.

funFact: Despite being invisible to the naked eye, this tiny algae is actually doing the same job as giant forest trees - capturing sunlight and carbon dioxide to make its own food through photosynthesis, producing oxygen that we breathe!
confusionNotes: **[UNCERTAIN: Confusion species]** Could be confused with other microscopic green algae in the same waters, but the specific cell shape and connection pattern require microscopic examination to distinguish reliably.
contextualKnowledge: This represents the often-overlooked microscopic world that exists all around us in New England's waters - thousands of species of algae, bacteria, and other microorganisms that form the foundation of aquatic food webs but remain invisible to most nature explorers.
compareHints: **[UNCERTAIN: Specific differences from related species]** Gonatozygon kinahanii differs from its relatives G. aculeatum, G. brebissonii, and G. pilosum primarily in cell wall details and connection structures that require microscopic examination to distinguish. All species in this genus share the basic cylindrical cell shape and aquatic lifestyle.
